The ESP32-S3 Mini Module is an ultra-compact embedded development module for IoT developers, makers and small electronics manufacturers. Built around a high-performance MCU, it integrates rich wireless connectivity and peripherals. While retaining a tiny footprint, it delivers strong computing power and flexible expansion — ideal for space-constrained smart devices and IoT applications.

ESP32-S3 dual-core 32-bit LX7 MCU, up to 240 MHz core frequency; 512 KB SRAM with hardware-accelerated float and vector instructions; Integrated neural-network accelerator (NPU) for INT8/FP16 AI inference (e.g. gesture recognition, simple image classification); Coprocessor support (RTC, UART, SPI peripherals run independently, reducing main-core load);

16 MB SPI NOR Flash (supports OTA firmware upgrade, large-application storage); 8 MB PSRAM (high-resolution image buffering, multi-task temp storage); External SPI storage expansion (up to 128 GB SD card); Encrypted firmware storage and secure boot (prevents tampering and reverse engineering);

For fast integration, the W16 (LR2021 RF module) and W11 (ESP32-S3 Mini Module) offer two connection methods: Method 1: Extension Board Connector Seat The W16 RF module ships with a board-to-board connector that plugs directly into the DF40C-30Pin socket on the W11 dev board for seamless mating and fast project start. Applicable regulations: This RF module is certified per FCC Part 15 Subpart C (intentional radiators). It is NOT certified under FCC Part 15 Subpart B (unintentional radiators); compliance of the host product falls to the end-equipment manufacturer. Basic operating limits: Rated supply: 3.3 V ~ 5.0 V DC. Over-voltage and reverse polarity are prohibited; Operating temperature: -40 ℃ ~ 85 ℃. Minimum safe distance between module antenna and human body: ≥ 20 cm; Do not stay in close proximity to the antenna region during device operation; This safety notice must appear in full on the end-product label and user manual;

Antenna types: internal ceramic + external IPEX (LR2021 uses IPEX-3, ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi/Bluetooth uses IPEX 1.0); Allowed antenna types: monopole, PIFA, dipole; Do not use non-certified third-party antennas or non-standard RF connectors; Antenna gain and impedance must stay within certified module parameters; otherwise certification is voided;

This RF module has been certified under the FCC Part 15.251 Limited Module Approval scheme. Host integrators must comply with the following procedures: The module may only be used on the certified hardware platform and antenna configuration. Do not assume FCC certification for new host platforms without additional testing. If the end product integrates this module with other RF transmitters (cellular, LoRa, 2.4 G Wi-Fi/BLE, etc.) operating concurrently, the host manufacturer must file an FCC Class II permissive change or perform a full new-device certification per Multi-Transmitter rules. Do not co-locate this module with other RF transmitters operating simultaneously unless a combined-transmitter evaluation and compliance has been completed. The host manufacturer is responsible for: (a) FCC Part 15 Subpart B (unintentional radiators) testing of the final host product; (b) the full compliance statement on the host label; (c) full recertification if the host contains uncertified RF transmitters operating concurrently.

FCC ID label requirements: The FCC ID label must be laser-engraved on the metal shield of the LR2021 RF module, minimum size 6 mm × 30 mm. Label format: FCC ID: 2BRTY-W16-V01. Text must be legible and remain readable after wear or reflection. If the module label is not externally visible when embedded in the host, a visible FCC ID label must be affixed in a prominent location on the host (front or bottom enclosure), or the module FCC ID and installation location must be clearly stated in the user manual. The label location diagram is provided by the module vendor and must not be altered. Additional label requirements for the host product: CE, RoHS and FCC marks must appear on both the product enclosure and the retail packaging, minimum mark size ≥ 3 mm. All marks must remain visible and legible during normal use and field servicing.

In the host PCB design, a continuous GND plane must be maintained beneath the module, with multiple vias connecting to the host main ground plane. Module power rails should use a series 10 µH ferrite bead and a 0.1 µF decoupling capacitor placed close to the module power pins. If the host enclosure is metal, maintain a minimum 5 mm clearance to the module antenna. Do not route copper within 2 mm of the module RF traces. The above routing requirements reference the Semtech LR2021 Hardware Design Guide. Violations may cause the host to fail FCC EMI testing.

Download and install the Arduino IDE Arduino download site: arduino.cc/en/software Download and install the software following the Arduino installation instructions Install the ESP32 Development Board To use ESP32-based boards in the Arduino IDE, you must first install the “esp32 by Espressif Systems” board package. After opening the software, install according to the panel installation requirements Add the development board manager URL Stable release link: https://espressif.github.io/arduino-esp32/package_esp32_index.json Development release link: https://espressif.github.io/arduino-esp32/package_esp32_dev_index.json When done, click OK Select Development Board Manager on the left side of the software Search for 'esp32' in the search bar In the version column of the ‘esp32 by Espressif Systems’ development board found in the search results, select version 3.2.0 or higher Click to install After clicking, a message like this will appear in the bottom-right corner of the software; please wait for the download to complete (ensure a stable network connection during the wait). After the download is complete, a success message will appear When you search again, 'Installed' will appear Development Board Type Configuration Development board type: XIAO_ESP32S3 Before each flashing, verify that the development board type is correct. Install Required Libraries When installing Arduino libraries, there are generally two options: online installation and offline installation. If a library requires offline installation, you must use the provided library files. For most libraries, users can easily search for and install them via the Arduino software's online library manager. However, some open-source or custom libraries are not synchronized with the Arduino library manager and cannot be obtained via online search. In such cases, users must install these libraries manually using the offline method. The library files for this product are already included in the example program compressed package, so there is no need to download additional libraries.

All example programs have their own .ino files, which you can modify based on the source code to achieve the expected results. There are also pre-compiled .bin files that can be flashed directly with flash_download_tool. The bin files ending with "merged" in each demo's "build" folder can be flashed directly.

Program Introduction This program verifies the LoRa receive capability of the W16 (ESP32-S3 + LR2021) dev board. It must be used together with the 02_tx transmit program. The receive frequency band can be switched online via serial commands without re-flashing the firmware. Main features include: Built-in three-band configurations: Sub-G 868MHz / 915MHz (BW125, SF12, CR4/5) and 2.4GHz 2450MHz (BW250, SF12, CR4/5) Supports serial (115200) online band switching: enter commands 868, 915, 2.4G (also supports 2400 / 2450 / 2.4) to switch; enter help or ? to print the command list Each time a packet is successfully received, the serial port outputs SeqNum, Band, Freq, BW, Power, RSSI, SNR information and accumulates the packet count On-board WS2812 RGB LED status indicator: green LED flashes once on successful packet reception, red LED flashes fast 3 times on read failure; green LED flashes twice on successful initialization, red LED flashes 10 times and halts on initialization failure Hardware Connection Connect the board to the computer with a USB cable If testing distance is long or signal is weak, it is recommended to connect a corresponding band antenna to the board's LoRa antenna connector Use together with the 02_tx transmit board; the band parameters on both ends must be exactly the same Performance 868rx serial output 915rx serial output 2.4rx serial output

Program Introduction This program verifies the LoRa transmit capability of the W16 (ESP32-S3 + LR2021) dev board. It must be used together with the 01_rx receive program. Transmit band and transmit power are both selected online via serial commands, making it convenient for comparative testing with the receive end at different rates and powers. Main features include: Built-in three-band configurations with corresponding power: Sub-G 868MHz / 915MHz (BW125, SF12, CR4/5, 22dBm); 2.4GHz 2450MHz (BW250, SF12, CR4/5, 12dBm, the hardware upper limit for 2.4G) Supports serial (115200) online band and power switching: enter 868, 915, 2.4G (also supports 2400 / 2450 / 2.4), enter help or ? to print the command list, commands are case-insensitive Over-the-air packet content is like hello <n> Sub-G 22dBm, where <n> is an incrementing counter; the receive end can use this to count packet loss rate On-board WS2812 RGB LED: blue LED stays on when idle, green LED flashes once on successful transmission, red LED flashes fast on failure Hardware Connection Connect the board to the computer with a USB cable It is recommended to connect a corresponding band antenna to the board's LoRa antenna connector (2.4G requires a 2.4G antenna) Use together with the 01_rx receive board; band, bandwidth, SF, and CR on both ends must be exactly the same Performance 868tx serial output 915tx serial output 2.4tx serial output

Program Introduction This program merges receive and transmit into a single firmware, switching between "receive mode" and "transmit mode" via serial commands for single-board self-test or dual-board pair testing (ping-pong) to verify the W16's LoRa link. Set one board to tx and the other to rx to form a minimal communication link, making it easy to quickly determine whether transmit/receive is normal and whether antenna and power are appropriate. Main features include: Three bands and two modes freely combined: 868rx / 915rx / 2.4rx switch band and enter receive; 868tx / 915tx / 2.4tx switch band and enter transmit; entering only 868 / 915 / 2.4g switches band only and keeps current mode Over-the-air packet is hello<n> (n increments); transmit log #<n> hello<n> Sub-G 868.0MHz OK, receive log #<n> Sub-G 868.0MHz RSSI=..dBm SNR=..dB Data: hello<n> On-board WS2812 RGB LED: green LED flash = transmit/receive success, blue LED stay-on = listening/idle, red LED fast flash = error Hardware Connection Connect the board to the computer with a USB cable (single-board self-test) or connect two boards separately with USB cables (dual-board pair testing) It is recommended to connect a corresponding band antenna to the board's LoRa antenna connector When testing with two boards, both boards must use the same band and the same rate parameters Performance 868tx & 868rx serial output 915tx & 915rx serial output 2.4tx & 2.4rx serial output

Program Introduction This program implements voice intercom based on the W16 (LR2021) FLRC 2.4GHz mode. The W16 module only has an RF chip, no microphone or speaker, and the ESP32-S3 itself has no codec either — so audio capture and playback are entirely handled by the mobile phone browser. The two dev boards only act as a wireless "audio bridge": board A receives phone microphone data via Wi-Fi and forwards it to the 2.4G FLRC air interface, board B receives it and forwards it to the phone webpage for playback. Main features include: Role assignment: board A mic (hotspot W16-MIC, forwards phone microphone data to the radio), board B spk (hotspot W16-SPK, receives packets, decodes to PCM for webpage playback) Serial commands (115200, newline terminated, case-insensitive): mic/tx, spk/rx, idle/stop, tone (board A sends built-in 1kHz tone), status (print stats), help Packet loss handling: receive end detects stream interruption based on seq and resets the decoder to avoid noise spread; send-on-demand (PTT semantics), stops sending packets when silent for 600ms Double buffering: board A ADPCM ring buffer 4096 bytes (~1 second margin) absorbs Wi-Fi jitter; board B PCM ring buffer 8000 samples (1 second, 16KB) 2.4G no router needed: phone connects directly to the dev board hotspot, opens webpage to intercom On-board WS2812 RGB LED: blue LED = listening/idle, red LED = transmitting, green LED flash = received a frame, off = idle, red LED fast flash = error Hardware Connection Connect the two boards separately to a computer or charger for power (board A is the mic end, board B is the spk end) Both boards need a 2.4GHz antenna (FLRC only supports 2.4G) and a Wi-Fi antenna Phone Wi-Fi connects to board A's hotspot W16-MIC (default password 12345678) for capture, connects to board B's hotspot W16-SPK (default password 12345678) for playback Note: Phone microphone requires a secure context. On Chrome/Android, add http://192.168.4.1 to chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure and restart the browser; iOS Safari does not have this switch and can only be used as the spk end Performance Board A (MIC) Phone connects to hotspot W16-MIC Open Chrome and go to chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure Restart the browser, go to http://192.168.4.1 Serial output (115200) Board B (SPK) Phone connects to hotspot W16-SPK Open browser, go to http://192.168.4.1 Serial output (115200)

Program Introduction This program implements image transmission over the W16 (LR2021) 2.4GHz FLRC link. Board A splits an image into small packets and sends them; board B reassembles them and provides webpage viewing through its own hotspot. The entire process does not require a router or internet. Main features include: Image packetization: each packet has 192 bytes of payload, max 255 blocks (~49KB buffer); the send end maintains a pending-send bitmap by block, the receive end maintains a received bitmap Multi-round retransmission mechanism: at the end of each round, board B returns the missing bitmap, board A only re-sends the missing blocks; default max 10 rounds, default block interval 4ms (increase if high packet loss), acknowledgment wait 700ms; if the acknowledgment itself is lost, the entire round is re-sent Dual roles and webpages: board A tx opens hotspot W16-SEND, phone can take a photo or select a local image to upload and send; board B rx opens hotspot W16-PHOTO, phone visits 192.168.4.1 to view received images Serial commands (115200): tx, rx, idle, send (immediately send current image), req (ask board A to re-send previous one), size X, gap N, rounds N, wifi, web (only open webpage hotspot to troubleshoot SSID), wtest (20-second hotspot test), ch N (hotspot channel, 0=stagger by role — board A 1/board B 5), power N (hotspot power 5/8/11/15/20dBm, default 15), clear (discard phone-uploaded image, use local capture instead), status, help BOOT button (GPIO0) can be used as board A's "immediately take photo and send" trigger On-board WS2812 RGB LED: blue LED = listening/idle, red LED = sending, green LED flash = received data frame, red LED fast flash = error Hardware Connection Connect the two boards separately to a computer or charger for power (board A is the send end, board B is the receive end) Both boards need a 2.4GHz antenna on the LoRa antenna connector (FLRC only supports 2.4G) Phone Wi-Fi connects to board A's hotspot W16-SEND (default password 12345678) to upload images; connect to board B's hotspot W16-PHOTO and visit 192.168.4.1 to view Performance Board A (SEND) Phone connects to hotspot W16-SEND Open browser, go to 192.168.4.1 Serial output (115200) Board B (PHOTO) Phone connects to hotspot W16-PHOTO Open browser, go to 192.168.4.1 Serial output (115200)

Program Introduction This program implements video transmission and real-time webpage preview over the W16 (LR2021) 2.4GHz FLRC link. Board A splits the video (camera or built-in animation) into fixed-length small packets and sends them continuously; board B reassembles them by frame and provides the latest frame for viewing by phone or computer browser through its own hotspot (visit 192.168.4.1). Main features include: Streaming strategy: no retransmission, no acknowledgment; lost blocks only affect the current frame, frame rate adapts dynamically with link quality, avoiding subsequent frame queuing caused by retransmission that makes the picture look stuck Fixed over-the-air frame 204 bytes: type, frameId, totalChunks, chunkIdx, format, flags, w, h, frameLen, data[192]; both transmit and receive ends must be consistent Dual roles and webpages: board A tx opens hotspot W16-CAM (control and local preview), board B rx opens hotspot W16-LIVE (watch live stream on webpage) Serial commands (115200): tx, rx, idle, send (single-frame debug), fps N (frame rate upper limit, default 4, 0=unlimited), gap N (packet interval, default 2ms, increase if high packet loss), pattern N (animation: 0 color bar / 1 bouncing square / 2 rainbow sweep), w N / h N (composed picture size, default 96×64, w×h ≤ 12288), size X (camera resolution), wifi (toggle hotspot), ch N (hotspot channel), status, help BOOT button (GPIO0) can be used as board A's shortcut key to toggle streaming On-board WS2812 RGB LED: blue LED = listening, red LED = streaming, green LED flash = received complete frame, off = idle, red LED fast flash = error Hardware Connection Connect the two boards separately to a computer or charger for power (board A is the send end, board B is the receive end) Both boards need a 2.4GHz antenna on the LoRa antenna connector (FLRC only supports 2.4G) Phone or computer Wi-Fi connects to board A's hotspot W16-CAM (default password 12345678) for preview and parameter adjustment; connect to board B's hotspot W16-LIVE and visit 192.168.4.1 to watch Performance Board A (CAM) Phone connects to hotspot W16-CAM Open browser, go to 192.168.4.1 Serial output (115200) Board B (LIVE) Phone connects to hotspot W16-LIVE Open browser, go to 192.168.4.1 ![] Serial output (115200)

A good LoRa or mesh board is only one part of a device you can take into the field. Getting started often meant finding a compatible enclosure, battery, antenna, and other components, then working out how to put them together. Meshnology began by making that process easier.

We first assembled complete kits around established boards, bringing the essential parts together in a practical setup. That experience showed us what matters when a device moves beyond the workbench: straightforward setup, practical power options, suitable antennas, and hardware designed for everyday use. Today, we continue to build kits around proven platforms while developing Meshnology hardware of our own. We support people who enjoy building, modifying, and experimenting, as well as those who want a more complete device they can take outside and use to connect with others.
